calibration.esm_if_bias_note: ESM-IF1 backbone encodes WT, so it is biased against all mutants; positive deltas are the informative signal
calibration.negative_controls_behave_correctly: I23E (ESM2 -11.81, ESM-IF -16.6 nats) and Y61E (ESM2 -9.95, ESM-IF -12.6 nats) both strongly penalized, confirming sign and scale

caveats: No measured assay outcome is reported or implied; all values are model scores.
The classical evolutionary channel (PSSM, Shannon conservation) is missing because no reference FASTA exists in the workspace - this is the single largest gap and a real MSA could reorder ranks 3-10.
ESM-2 and ESM-IF1 are both ESM-family models and are correlated; agreement between them is weaker evidence than two truly independent channels.
No burial/secondary-structure measurement (dssp failed on the ESMFold artifact), so all buried-vs-exposed reasoning is inferred, not measured.
Ranks 1-2 (D33E, R51K) are meaningfully better supported than ranks 3-10; the tail is a low-risk-filler tier, not a set of confident positives.
TM-align does not discriminate here: all three refolds scored TM 0.97-0.996 vs WT, so fold retention alone did not separate good from bad candidates - only pLDDT and ESM-IF1 did.

rejected_channel_disagreement_trusting_s.rationale: ESM-2 rates these neutral-to-positive (F17A +0.08, S18F +0.02, A49L +0.53) but ESM-IF1 penalizes them heavily (-7.5 to -15.7 nats), the signature of cavity creation / packing loss at buried sites that a sequence-only model misses. F17A was refolded as a direct test: fold is retained (TM 0.971 vs WT) but pLDDT drops to 0.864, the largest decrease of any refold performed, corroborating the structure channel. Note A49L has the single highest ESM-2 score among rejects and is the strongest candidate to promote if burial at position 49 turns out to be low - an MSA or dssp run would decide.

answer.evidence_gaps: blast_msa/blast_search/mmseqs_search require an existing workspace reference FASTA; none exists, so pssm_score and conservation could not be run - the classical evolutionary channel is entirely absent. dssp rejects the ESMFold artifact (no valid PDB HEADER), so no measured burial/secondary structure; burial is inferred indirectly from ESM-IF1 penalties. Both remaining scoring channels are ESM-family and therefore correlated, not fully independent.
answer.method: All 100 candidates scored with ESM-2 650M masked marginals (delta log-prob, nats). Top tier cross-checked with ESM-IF1 conditioned on the ESMFold WT backbone (WT baseline mean LL -1.31343, native_sequence_match=true; delta reported as total nats over 69 residues). Generic BLOSUM62 added as a protein-independent sanity check. Top 2 picks plus the main rejected disagreement case were refolded and TM-aligned to WT. Consensus score = ESM2_delta + ESM_IF_delta_total.
answer.objective_assumed: No assay objective was specified; ranked for highest probability of being tolerated / mildly beneficial for fold and function. These are PREDICTIONS only - no measured assay outcome is claimed or implied.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Only candidate clearly positive in BOTH learned channels. Conservative acidic-to-acidic swap. Refold keeps pLDDT 0.885 (identical to WT) and TM 0.971 / RMSD 0.73 A vs WT.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: A real MSA showing D33 strictly invariant (e.g. a metal/DNA-contact or salt-bridge partner where the extra methylene misplaces the carboxylate); or a measured loss of function despite conserved fold.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Highest ESM-2 score of all 100 candidates (+1.91; mutant log-prob -0.14 vs WT -2.05, i.e. ESM-2 prefers K over R here). ESM-IF1 also positive despite WT bias. Refold is nearly identical to WT: TM 0.996, RMSD 0.19 A, pLDDT 0.880.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: If R51 makes a bidentate arginine-specific contact (DNA phosphate/guanine or a buried salt bridge) that lysine cannot replace - exactly the kind of specificity BLOSUM and sequence models blur. A DNA-binding assay would test this directly.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Second-highest ESM-2 score (+1.21); ESM-IF1 penalty is negligible (-0.011 mean LL). ESM-2 assigns WT G21 a low probability (-3.11), i.e. glycine is not the model's preferred residue at this site.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: If G21 is a required backbone-flexibility hinge (it sits just before the E22-I23-V24 segment), any beta-branched/larger side chain could rigidify it; DSSP/phi-psi at position 21 would settle this and was NOT obtainable here.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Near-neutral in ESM-2 and positive in ESM-IF1; conservative E-to-D in the C-terminal tail, a low-constraint region. Low-risk queue filler.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: Involvement of E66 in a C-terminal capping interaction where shortening the side chain breaks an H-bond; low prior, low information either way.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Second-largest positive ESM-IF1 delta (backbone tolerates K at 53 well). Conservative charge-preserving swap.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: Channel conflict: ESM-2 mildly disfavours it (-1.18), and ESM-2 rates WT R53 highly (-0.34), hinting at evolutionary constraint. An MSA showing R53 invariant would demote this; same arginine-specific-contact caveat as R51K.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Positive ESM-IF1 delta, suggesting position 25 is solvent-exposed enough to accept a larger polar side chain; ESM-2 penalty is mild.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: A25 sits in the A25-A26-L27 stretch; if it is in fact partly buried, Gln introduces a desolvation penalty that ESM-IF1's backbone-only view can miss. Burial measurement (dssp) was unavailable - this is the weakest structural assumption in the top 6.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Essentially neutral on the structure channel (delta +0.03 nats) with only a mild ESM-2 penalty; adjacent to the well-tolerated R51/R53 sites.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: Loss of a Thr hydroxyl H-bond or helix-capping role; also a polar-to-hydrophobic change on a likely exposed face could promote aggregation, which neither channel models.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Both learned channels near-neutral despite a strongly negative BLOSUM62 (-3), a case where generic substitution scoring and context-aware models disagree and the context-aware models should win. ESM-2 gives WT C62 a low probability (-3.79), so the lone cysteine is not model-preferred. High information: C62 is the only Cys in the protein, so this tests whether it matters at all.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: Any role for C62 as a metal ligand or in a cross-link/redox function would make this severely deleterious - BLOSUM -3 is a genuine warning I am partly discounting. Rank 8 reflects that residual risk.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Small penalties in both channels; position 3 is in the flexible N-terminal region where constraint is lowest. Conservative isosteric charge-neutralizing change.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: Little - this is a low-risk, low-information pick included to fill the queue rather than to test a hypothesis. A strong N-terminal electrostatic requirement would overturn it.

ranked_selection.supporting_evidence: Almost exactly neutral on ESM-2 (-0.10), which also rates WT M59 only -2.92, so methionine is weakly preferred at this site. Modest ESM-IF1 penalty.
ranked_selection.what_would_overturn: The ESM-IF1 penalty (-2.0 nats) plus BLOSUM -2 suggests M59 may contribute hydrophobic packing in the C-terminal M57-E58-M59-V60-Y61 stretch; if buried, M-to-N would be destabilizing. Ranked last of the ten for this reason.
